text:
ben (sales): Heads-up, Acme demo POC is showing a bunch of 503s when we ramp past ~90 rps. Demo starts in 50m. @olivia @maya can we triage?

olivia (support): On it. Can you paste a failing request id and the client concurrency / setup? Also are they on Hosted or Dedicated?

ben (sales): Req id: req_02B7C1Y. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate model=gptx-6.7b-quant. Client concurrency ~12 (3 threads x 4). Hosted POC. Error snippet: "{"error":"resource busy"}". Seems to spike after sustained ramp for ~20s.

maya (sre): Pulling runtime logs now. Two quick asks: did you enable burstpool and any fallback routing? Any custom per-route concurrency overrides?

ben (sales): Route config copied from demo README: 
``
route: /v1/generate
model: gptx-6.7b-quant
burstpool: enabled
max_concurrency_per_instance: 8
fallback: none
``

maya (sre): Logs show rapid queue growth then immediate 503s before autoscaler could spin up. Snip: 
``
[2026-03-21T15:10:12Z] runtime accept req=req_02B7C1Y
[2026-03-21T15:10:13Z] runtime queue_depth=96 -> burstpool_alloc(24)
[2026-03-21T15:10:14Z] runtime kernel oom on quant path
[2026-03-21T15:10:14Z] runtime respond 503 capacity_exceeded
[2026-03-21T15:10:44Z] autoscaler scale_up trigger delta=1 nodes delay=30s
[2026-03-21T15:11:05Z] nodes healthy
```
Looks like a combination of short autoscale convergence and quant OOMs when burstpool hands off too many queued requests.

olivia (support): Short-term options: 1) route a canary to a smaller variant (gptx-6.7b-fast) to absorb spikes, 2) temporarily lower max_concurrency_per_instance to 6 to reduce OOMs, 3) pre-warm an extra node / bump burstpool reserve, 4) advise client to add jittered backoff for retries. I can apply the canary change now.

deploy-bot: rollout started: route /v1/generate updated -> fallback gptx-6.7b-fast (canary=15%) by olivia (support)

maya (sre): I'll request a one-off capacity bump to pre-warm + add a temporary autoscale policy with faster scale_up. Pre-warm ETA ~6m. Also dropping a quick config note to demo README about lowering in-flight concurrency for quant models.

ben (sales): Quick pricing question from Acme: will the extra pre-warm or burst GPU time for the demo cause a surprise invoice? They want to avoid surprises for a short demo.

jack (finance): For a 1hr demo with a single pre-warm node, it's minor — roughly $100-200 of additional GPU time depending on region and instance type. We can provide a capped demo credit for proof-of-value if needed. For production sustained usage we'd recommend reserved capacity pricing.

olivia (support): Created SR SR-5121 with log bundle and the recommended route patch. I've also added a small step-by-step for client-side pacing to the demo README and pasted it into the SR.

maya (sre): Canary metrics: after ~4m the 503 rate for the route dropped from ~10% to 1.2%. Kernel OOMs reduced after we dropped per-instance concurrency on the canary variant. Extra node healthy and serving. I'm monitoring for another 10m before flipping to 100% if stable.

ben (sales): Good news, Acme engineer reports latency back to expected and demo team can proceed. Please post postmortem notes and config patch in the SR so we can share with the customer. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

olivia (support): Will do. Follow-ups: 1) recommend a permanent fallback model or quantization profile for demos, 2) doc the demo runbook with pre-warm + client pacing, 3) offer a time-limited demo credit to Acme to cover the extra GPU time. I'll update SR-5121 with all items.

maya (sre): Adding one more ops note: autoscaler defaults are tuned for steady-state; for demo/ramp scenarios consider a faster aggressive scale policy or pre-warm hooks. Filing infra ticket to expose demo-friendly autoscale preset.

ben (sales): Perfect. Ping when SR updated and when you've flipped canary to full and closed the loop with Acme.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: fallback gptx-6.7b-fast promoted to 100% (applied by olivia)
